title: Suitability and quality of the measures to maximise expected outcomes and impacts, as set out in the dissemination and exploitation plan, including communication activities
content:
Sub-section 2.2 — Suitability and quality of the measures to maximise expected outcomes and impacts, as set out in the dissemination and exploitation plan, including communication activities

Overall strategy and proportionality to a single-researcher action. FIELDWISE treats dissemination, exploitation and communication as one continuous, planned strand rather than an end-loaded afterthought. The work plan carries a dedicated cross-cutting dissemination/exploitation strand alongside the training/two-way-transfer strand and the management/Open Science/IP strand, running across the whole action and resourced from the fellow's cross-cutting person-month allocation. Because this is a single-researcher fellowship executed by Dr. Rositsa Cholakova, every measure below is deliberately sized to what one fellow, supported by the host HUN-REN Agrartudomanyi Kutatokozpont and the associated and partner organisations, can credibly deliver and sustain — a focused set of high-quality outputs and well-targeted audience actions rather than an over-scaled campaign. The whole strand is governed by the Open Science principle "as open as possible, as closed as necessary": methods, metadata and publications are made reusable wherever possible, while any potentially protectable foreground is evaluated before public disclosure. This proportionate, front-to-back design is what allows the modest resource of a single postdoctoral action to still generate scientific, practitioner-facing and industrial impact.

Target groups. The plan addresses five distinct groups, each with a matched channel: (i) the scientific and professional research community in plant-stress physiology, agricultural data science, remote sensing/Earth observation and precision agriculture; (ii) growers, farm advisors and the wider agricultural sector, particularly in the two countries FIELDWISE works in, Hungary and Bulgaria; (iii) the agricultural-software and farm-management-information-system (FMIS) industry, together with precision-agriculture and irrigation-technology companies, Earth-observation/geospatial organisations and crop-phenotyping groups, as the exploitation-relevant audience; (iv) students and the higher-education community; and (v) the general public and policy-relevant audiences, framed through the project's contribution to SDG 2, SDG 6, SDG 12 and SDG 13. Naming the groups explicitly lets each activity be judged on fit rather than on volume.

Dissemination to scientific and professional audiences. Scientific dissemination is built around at least two high-quality peer-reviewed submissions during or shortly after the fellowship: P1 on physiologically grounded water-stress signatures derived from the heterogeneous MATE archive, and P2 on modelling, uncertainty and the transfer from historical experiments to prospective commercial-field validation; a third methods/application paper on multi-scale UAV/Sentinel operationalisation and DrR is prepared if the independent dataset supports it. These are complemented by conference presentations and by seminars in the MATE, HUN-REN and ELTE environments. Dissemination is delivered under Open Science discipline in line with the call's training requirement: open access to publications, and FAIR, reusable methods and metadata, including the registered model card of the Primary model, benchmark and model card and the Stress-target, feature-selection and validation protocol, and the harmonised datasets and variable-availability map where institutional permissions allow. Crucially, the project commits to reporting transfer honestly — the Prospective transferability, uncertainty and limited-recalibration report (due month 18) treats any performance drop under prospective validation as a scientific result to be quantified rather than hidden — which is itself a form of high-integrity dissemination. This directly serves the call's expected outcome of enhanced networking and communication capacities with scientific peers (EO-03) and the corresponding expected impact of increased and broadened R&I impact (EI-02), and it feeds the stronger R&I capacity and better knowledge transfer among participating organisations (EI-05) through the model card, the Spectral/UAV/Sentinel harmonisation and crop-transfer specification (due month 14) and the two-way transfer between the fellow and the ATK/ELTE/MATE environments.

Communication to practitioners, students and the public. Communication is deliberately widened beyond research audiences. The fellow will deliver practitioner-oriented demonstrations of the stress and uncertainty outputs; Krumatic supports Bulgarian farmer-facing dissemination, demonstration and uptake of the MVP, providing a concrete channel into the Bulgarian grower community. As an operator-preserved commitment, the project targets one public field demonstration with farmers and one public-facing article per year. Only if it is formally established and scientifically suitable, a public-facing demonstration at the planned Szentendre Skanzen model Bulgarian garden would link traditional horticultural knowledge with modern environmental sensing; this is stated conditionally and carries no unconditional promise. Teaching-linked communication — short guest lectures, seminars or practical sessions at MATE and, where institutionally possible, the Agricultural University of Plovdiv — feeds research results back into higher education. Together these activities address broadened public engagement (EI-03) and the feedback of results into teaching (EI-06), while remaining sized to a single fellow's realistic reach.

Exploitation plan. Exploitation is anchored in a tangible research-to-application vehicle: the crop-configurable DrR web MVP with validated processing-tomato module (due month 24), which provides a concrete route from validated research to external testing while preserving the distinction between the fellow's pre-existing DrR background and the FIELDWISE foreground. Because the MVP is completed before the M25-M30 placement, the non-academic placement at AgroVIR is genuine evaluation and transfer rather than first build: it yields the AgroVIR operational/interoperability assessment (due month 30) covering MVP inputs, usability, missing-data behaviour, decision outputs, workflow compatibility and interoperability requirements, and the Post-MSCA FMIS integration and exploitation roadmap (due month 30), which names the required interfaces, the exploitation route and the post-fellowship steps. The architecture is crop-configurable by design: within the action, validation is confined to processing tomato, and the Spectral/UAV/Sentinel harmonisation and crop-transfer specification defines the transferable core components, crop-specific parameters, minimum validation datasets and recalibration gates any later crop addition must pass — so exploitation beyond tomato is presented as a scientifically controlled pathway, not an unsupported universalisation. Economic value is deliberately not expressed as an invented EUR/ha or fixed water-saving promise; instead the project quantifies the measured quantities — irrigation water applied, water productivity, yield and marketable yield, quality indicators, intervention timing and warning lead time — from which later economic value can be assessed. A defined post-MSCA replication route through MVCRI transfers and re-validates the outcomes on additional tomato cultivars under Bulgarian production conditions as knowledge transfer outside the 24-month work plan (no in-action MVCRI effort is claimed). This inter-sectoral, cross-border exploitation logic instantiates the call's expected impact of stimulated innovation and knowledge transfer and expanded career opportunities through the non-academic placement incentive (EI-05) and reinforces the fellow's employability across academic and non-academic destinations (EI-01). The delivery of the reachable web MVP, the completion of the external AgroVIR evaluation and the definition of the integration path give the plan three concrete, verifiable exploitation checkpoints.

Intellectual-property management and foreseen protection measures. IP is managed on a separate-rights-layers doctrine established at the outset. At project start, HUN-REN ATK, ELTE, MATE, Krumatic, AgroVIR and the fellow establish an inventory of relevant background datasets, software, code, methods and other assets, and this background/foreground inventory is maintained throughout the action as an explicit task and used to define the post-MSCA exploitation route. Four rights layers are kept distinct and each documented before the action starts: the fellow's pre-existing DrR background; the FIELDWISE scientific foreground; institutional datasets; and Krumatic-developed code. The fellow's DrR background is stated to have been initiated and developed independently using her own time and personal financial resources, with no MVCRI ownership position — a position to be confirmed in writing and hardened by a dated background declaration and version inventory before the action starts. Protection measures are proportionate and staged: potentially protectable foreground is evaluated before public disclosure under the "as closed as necessary" limb; MATE data are used only for the approved scientific purposes of FIELDWISE under institutional data-use conditions to be documented before the action starts, and any use of MATE-derived models or institutional assets in a future marketable product is subject to a separate legal and institutional data-rights/IP assessment before commercial exploitation. Code-IP terms for the FIELDWISE code (ownership or sufficient exploitation rights) are to be settled in a Krumatic development agreement concluded before the action starts. For the placement, ownership of results is to follow the grant-agreement default, vesting in HUN-REN ATK as beneficiary acting through the fellow, with a written placement agreement between the fellow, HUN-REN ATK and AgroVIR — concluded before the placement begins — confirming this allocation and the access terms to the DrR background; the placement itself is conducted mainly through remote collaboration, with AgroVIR supplying only protected, coded or anonymised data extracts (for example "Field X" identifiers) so that no access to proprietary customer databases or production systems is required. Farmer and AgroVIR operational information is minimised and coded/anonymised where appropriate, and results are published only in aggregated, coded or anonymised form. Several of these arrangements (MATE data rights, the placement IP allocation and the placement data arrangement) rest on operator declarations pending partner writing and are presented as such rather than as settled fact; the IP framework nevertheless gives the evaluator a complete, layered protection design rather than a gap.

Concrete actions during and after the project, and overall proportionality. During the action, the measures are embodied in named, resourced activities: the continuous dissemination/exploitation strand; the maintained background/foreground/IP inventory; structured AgroVIR requirements consultation from month 1; the DrR web MVP and its pre-placement usability/interoperability dossier; annual public-facing communication; and the placement's operational evaluation. After the action, continuity is secured by the Post-MSCA FMIS integration and exploitation roadmap, the MVCRI Bulgarian replication route, the crop-transfer specification enabling later crop modules after crop-specific validation, and publications appearing during or shortly after the fellowship. All of this is scaled to a single-researcher MSCA Postdoctoral Fellowship: a compact, high-quality output set with clearly matched target groups and verifiable checkpoints, delivering scientific, practitioner and industrial impact without over-committing the resources of one fellow.

claim_statuses.claim_summary: Dissemination/exploitation is a dedicated continuous cross-cutting strand across the whole action, resourced from the fellow's cross-cutting person-months, run as a single-researcher action.
The D&E&C strand is governed by 'as open as possible, as closed as necessary', with reusable methods/metadata/publications and pre-disclosure evaluation of protectable foreground.
Target groups: scientific/professional community; growers and agricultural sector (Hungary/Bulgaria); FMIS/precision-ag/EO/crop-phenotyping industry; students; general public/SDG audiences.
At least two peer-reviewed submissions P1 and P2 during or shortly after the fellowship, plus a third methods/application paper if the independent dataset supports it.
Dissemination under open access and FAIR reusable methods/metadata, including the registered model card and the validation protocol.
Transfer loss is reported honestly as a scientific result in the Prospective transferability, uncertainty and limited-recalibration report (due month 18).
Dissemination measures serve EO-03 (networking/communication capacities), EI-02 (broadened R&I impact) and EI-05 (stronger R&I capacity and knowledge transfer).
Communication includes practitioner demonstrations, one public field demonstration and one public-facing article per year, and Krumatic-supported Bulgarian farmer-facing dissemination/uptake.
A public-facing Szentendre Skanzen demonstration is included only if the garden is formally established and suitable (conditional).
Short guest lectures/seminars/practical sessions at MATE and, where possible, the Agricultural University of Plovdiv feed results into teaching (EI-06/EO-08).
Communication activities address EI-03 (broadened public engagement).
Exploitation is anchored in the Crop-configurable DrR web MVP with validated processing-tomato module (due month 24) as a research-to-external-testing route.
The MVP is completed before the M25-M30 placement, making the AgroVIR placement evaluation/transfer yielding the AgroVIR operational/interoperability assessment (due month 30).
The Post-MSCA FMIS integration and exploitation roadmap (due month 30) names required interfaces, the exploitation route and post-fellowship steps.

The Spectral/UAV/Sentinel harmonisation and crop-transfer specification (due month 14) defines transferable core, crop-specific parameters and recalibration gates for controlled extension beyond tomato.
Economic value is not expressed as an invented EUR/ha or fixed water-saving promise; the project quantifies measured quantities from which later value can be assessed.
A defined post-MSCA MVCRI Bulgarian replication route transfers/re-validates outcomes outside the 24-month plan with no in-action MVCRI effort claimed.
Inter-sectoral, cross-border exploitation instantiates EI-05 and reinforces EI-01 (employability within academia and beyond).

A background/foreground/IP inventory is established and maintained (T4.6); four distinct rights layers (DrR background, FIELDWISE foreground, institutional datasets, Krumatic code) are documented before the action starts.

DrR - Digital Agronomist was initiated and developed by the fellow independently, using her own time and personal financial resources; it was not commissioned or financed by MVCRI, and MVCRI holds no ownership position in it.

Protection measures: protectable foreground evaluated before disclosure; DrR background documented/deposited with a dated declaration; institutional data-rights/IP assessment before commercial exploitation (R10).

MATE grants the project rights and access to the 2022-2026 processing-tomato archive for the approved scientific purposes of FIELDWISE, with experimental metadata, under institutional data-use conditions to be documented before the action starts.
Use of MATE-derived models/assets in a future marketable product is subject to separate legal and institutional data-rights/IP assessment.
Code-IP terms for FIELDWISE code are settled in a Krumatic development agreement concluded before the action starts.

Ownership of placement results follows the grant agreement default, vesting in HUN-REN ATK as the beneficiary acting through the fellow; a written placement agreement between the fellow, HUN-REN ATK and AgroVIR, concluded before the placement begins, will confirm this allocation and the access terms to the fellow's DrR background IP.

The M25-M30 placement is conducted mainly through remote collaboration with monthly face-to-face technical meetings for review, feedback and progress assessment. The fellow does not require direct access to AgroVIR's proprietary software, customer databases, office infrastructure or computing equipment; AgroVIR provides the information and data extracts required for interoperability testing in protected form (coded or anonymised field identifiers, e.g. 'Field X'). The fellow works with the AgroVIR product development team responsible for the FMIS platform.
Farmer and AgroVIR operational information is minimised and coded/anonymised, and results are published only in aggregated, coded or anonymised form.

Concrete during-project actions (inventory, AgroVIR consultation from M1, MVP, dossier, annual communication, placement evaluation) and after-project continuity (roadmap, MVCRI replication, crop-transfer extension, publications).
